input.prompt: Simulate uniaxial tensile loading of an Aluminum single crystal oriented in the <100> direction using LAMMPS. The simulation should use a face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice structure for Aluminum with a lattice constant of 4.05 Å, aligned along the <100> directions in x, y, and z. Define a 10×10×10 simulation box with periodic boundary conditions (PBCs) in all directions. Equilibrate this initial lattice using the NPT ensemble to reach a temperature of 300 K while maintaining a pressure of 0 bar in all directions. Initialize atomic velocities using a Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution at 300 K. Run the equilibration for at least 20 picoseconds (ps) with a timestep of 0.001 picoseconds (ps) to ensure system stability. After equilibration, apply uniaxial tension along the x-direction at a strain rate of 0.01 picosecond⁻¹. The y and z directions should be controlled using the NPT equations of motion while maintaining zero pressure. Continue the deformation process for 20 ps to observe the material's response. Save stress and strain values to a text file every 100 timesteps. The output should include strain, defined as (Lx - L0)/L0, and stress values in the x, y, and z directions, converted from bars to GPa. Generate a stress-strain curve plot and save it as an image file. The final output should return the absolute path of the text file containing the stress-strain data.

Initialize a 3D Aluminum single crystal in LAMMPS. Use metal units and define a 10×10×10 simulation box in three dimensions. Create a face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice with a lattice constant of 4.05 Å, oriented in the <100> directions along x, y, and z. Set periodic boundary conditions in all directions. Define the atomic type for Aluminum and assign the atomic structure inside the simulation box. Save this structure using the write_data command in LAMMPS data format. As the final output, return the absolute path of the structure file.

You are given the absolute path of the initialized structure of the 3D Aluminum single crystal. Read that structure file and equilibrate the system using an NPT ensemble at a temperature of 300 K and a pressure of 0 bar in all directions. Initialize atomic velocities using a Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution at 300 K. Run the equilibration for 20 picoseconds with a timestep of 0.001 picoseconds. Save the equilibrated structure in LAMMPS data format using the write_data command, and as the final output, return its absolute path.

You are given the absolute path of the equilibrated structure of the 3D Aluminum single crystal. Read that structure file and apply uniaxial tensile deformation along the x-direction at a strain rate of 0.01 picosecond⁻¹ using the fix deform command. Maintain zero pressure in the y and z directions using the NPT ensemble. Run the simulation for 20 picoseconds with a timestep of 0.001 picoseconds. Save the stress and strain data to a text file every 100 timesteps. As the final output, return the absolute path of this text file.
